recall.question: B1: Write the forward transition and name the two quantities controlling one step.
recall.answer: q(x_t | x_{t-1}) = N(sqrt(1 - beta_t) x_{t-1}, beta_t I). The shrinkage sqrt(1 - beta_t) and the noise variance beta_t.

recall.question: B4: Which ELBO term is dropped during training and why?
recall.answer: L_T is dropped because p_theta(x_T) is fixed N(0, I), so it carries no parameters.

sections.title: Deep ladder D1, forward process (5 follow-ups)

keyTerms.definition: Transition density, the beta schedule, and alpha-bar_t.
Linear maps of Gaussians stay Gaussian.

recall.question: D1.2: Give alpha-bar_50 and the mean and std of x_50.
D1.3: Why is x_t given x_0 Gaussian with variance 1 - alpha-bar_t?
recall.answer: Linear maps of Gaussians stay Gaussian; independent noise variances add; the telescoping sum gives exactly 1 - alpha-bar_t.

sections.title: Deep ladder D2, ELBO and sampling (5 follow-ups)

keyTerms.definition: log p_theta(x_0) >= E_q[log p_theta(x_0:T) / q(x_1:T | x_0)].
From (14.19) to (14.22) by substitution.
Loss near zero with bad samples: the network fit the wrong target.

recall.question: D2.2: Compute x_50 and the unweighted loss.
D2.3: Derive the noise form (14.22) from (14.19).
recall.answer: Substitute x_0 = (x_t - sqrt(1 - alpha-bar_t) epsilon) / sqrt(alpha-bar_t) from (14.5) into (14.19), simplify with alpha-bar_t = alpha_t alpha-bar_{t-1}.

keyTerms.definition: beta_t (1 - alpha-bar_{t-1}) / (1 - alpha-bar_t) < beta_t.
grad_x log q(x_t | x_0) = -epsilon-hat_t / sqrt(1 - alpha-bar_t).

recall.question: Q1: Prove beta-tilde_t < beta_t and give its value at t = 50.
recall.answer: beta-tilde_t = beta_t (1 - alpha-bar_{t-1}) / (1 - alpha-bar_t) < beta_t. Numeric: beta-tilde_50 = 0.00960, beta_50 = 0.00995.

recall.question: Q2: Derive the score relation.
recall.answer: grad_x log q(x_t | x_0) = -epsilon-hat_t / sqrt(1 - alpha-bar_t).

keyTerms.definition: Must be sqrt(beta_tilde_t), not sqrt(beta_t).
Noise added at t = 1; must be xi = 0 at the final step.

recall.question: T1: Identify the two bugs in the reverse sampling loop.
recall.answer: Bug 1: the noise scale is sqrt(beta_t); the notes fix sigma_t^2 = beta-tilde_t. Bug 2: noise is added at t = 1; the notes set xi = 0 at the final step.

keyTerms.definition: The small-step assumption breaks; learn the variance or use DDIM-style.
Categorical forward transition or absorbing-state diffusion.

recall.question: S1: What breaks with 20 reverse steps instead of 1000?
recall.answer: The small-step assumption breaks: each reverse kernel must cover a large denoising jump. Fixes: learn the variance, use a few-step schedule, or switch to a deterministic DDIM-style sampler.

recall.question: S2: What replaces the Gaussian forward chain for discrete tokens?
recall.answer: Discrete diffusion with a categorical forward transition (masking or uniform corruption), or absorbing-state diffusion.

keyTerms.definition: Lower training loss but worse FID does not imply overfitting.
Exact weighted held-out ELBO plus FID on the same held-out set.

recall.question: R1: Is the baseline-overfitting conclusion sound?
recall.answer: No. Training loss is the unweighted denoising objective; FID is perceptual. Decide with one experiment: exact weighted held-out ELBO and FID on the same held-out set.
